claims.text: The Co-free FeNiCrMn alloy is in a solidified solid-solution state.
The dynamic behavior of Co-free FeNiCrMn across temperature and strain rate is governed by temperature-dependent activation of dislocation glide.
The solid-solution state and atomic-scale lattice distortions influence dislocation glide.
At lower temperatures, lattice distortions hinder dislocation glide.
Hindered dislocation glide at lower temperatures produces higher strength.
Hindered dislocation glide at lower temperatures produces reduced ductility.
At higher temperatures, thermal activation facilitates dislocation glide.
Thermally facilitated dislocation glide at higher temperatures reduces strength.
Thermally facilitated dislocation glide at higher temperatures improves ductility.
Strain-rate sensitivity arises from interactions between dislocations and lattice obstacles that vary with strain rate.
The alloy's strength will decrease as temperature rises.
The alloy's ductility will increase as temperature rises.
Higher strain rates will produce higher strength.
Higher strain rates will produce lower ductility.
Temperature- and strain-rate-dependent effects will be less pronounced in Co-free FeNiCrMn than in equiatomic CoCrFeMnNi.
Removing Co reduces stacking-fault energy relative to CoCrFeMnNi.
Removing Co alters dislocation behavior relative to CoCrFeMnNi.
The proposed mechanism applies from approximately -150°C to 600°C and from strain rates of approximately 10^-3 s^-1 to 10^3 s^-1.
The proposed behavior is limited to Co-free FeNiCrMn alloys in a solid-solution state and may differ in the presence of secondary phases or significant compositional deviations.
A controlled comparison should test Co-free FeNiCrMn and equiatomic CoCrFeMnNi under identical temperatures and strain rates while measuring strength, ductility, and strain-rate sensitivity.
